dĭdascălĭcus , a, um, adj., = διδασκαλικός,
I.pertaining to instruction, didactic (ante- and post-class.): “opusculum,” Aus. Ep. 17 .—Subst.: Dĭdascălica , ōn or ōrum, n., the title of a work by Attius, in Gell. 3, 11, 4 al.; cf. Madvig Opuscc. Acadd. prior. pp. 87-110.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
